notes: Order and label set mirror berigold (least touristy, underrated, unique, diverse, delicious, romantic, ..., peaceful, relaxing, beaches, everything-in-one). Two labels adapted: berigold's 'most colorful' became Koh Tao 'הכי שווה ללמוד לצלול' (no source calls any Thai island the most colourful; Tao's dive-school claim is sourced), and 'most spectacular beaches' is written 'החופים הכי יפים' because that is how it is said in Hebrew. 'הכל במקום אחד' has no הכי because 'הכי הכל במקום אחד' is not Hebrew. Phuket is in for 'הכי טעים' because it is the only island with an official food title (UNESCO City of Gastronomy, 2015, first in ASEAN); the UNESCO title is for Phuket City but UNESCO's own page describes the island. Koh Chang (Trat), Lanta, Lipe, Samet and Phangan were left out to keep 11. Every quote was checked as a verbatim substring of the page fetched on 10.10.2026 (curly apostrophes as on the page; the space before the period in 'Ko Chang .' is how the Rough Guides page renders a link). Caveats: travelfish calls Phi Phi overdeveloped in the next sentence and Samui 'not somewhere to come to glimpse a corner of the Thai kingdom untouched by mass tourism' - the quotes are positive excerpts, which is fine for 'beaches' and 'everything' but do not quote further. Koh Muk is called 'the busiest of Trang province's islands' by travelfish - so 'הכי מיוחד' rests on the Emerald Cave, not on quietness. Koh Libong vs Ko Sukorn: travelfish says Sukorn is even quieter, but Sukorn has almost no Unsplash photos and Libong is the one with sources saying 'least visited'. Kradan's Rough Guides entry also warns of a midday rush of day-trip boats. Spelling uncertain: קו פיאם (also seen as קו פאיאם), קו מוק (English sources split Muk/Mook),קוסמוי (Israelis also write קוסמוי as one word). Unsplash coverage is thin for Libong, Mak, Phayam and Kradan; if the island query returns nothing good, verify any look-alike photo is really that island before using it. Koh Nang Yuan (photo query for Tao) is a separate islet joined to Koh Tao by boat - it is the classic Koh Tao view but say 'קו טאו' only if the frame is acceptable to him.
